blogs.title: Stop Asking the LLM Every Time: How FeatLLM Turns GPT Into a Feature Engineer
blogs.description: This post would introduce the paper’s central idea in plain language: instead of using a large language model to make every prediction directly, FeatLLM uses it once to create useful rules and features for tabular data. It would explain why this shift matters for speed, cost, and real-world deployment, especially in low-data settings.

blogs.title: Few-Shot Learning for Spreadsheets: Why LLMs Can Help When You Only Have a Handful of Rows
blogs.description: This article would focus on the few-shot tabular learning problem: what it is, why traditional models often struggle with very small labeled datasets, and how LLM prior knowledge can fill in the gaps. It would use relatable examples from healthcare, finance, and business data to show why FeatLLM performs well with only a few examples.

blogs.title: From Natural Language to Prediction Rules: A Simple Walkthrough of How FeatLLM Works
blogs.description: This post would break down the method step by step for non-specialists. It would explain how the system prompts an LLM to reason about a task, generate class-specific rules, convert those rules into binary features, and then train a lightweight model on top. The emphasis would be on making the pipeline understandable without requiring a machine learning background.

blogs.title: Why FeatLLM Beats End-to-End LLM Prediction on Tabular Data
blogs.description: This post would compare FeatLLM with other LLM-based tabular approaches like in-context prediction and fine-tuned models. It would highlight the paper’s claims about lower inference cost, API-only access, better scalability to many columns, and stronger average performance, helping readers understand why the approach is practically appealing.

blogs.title: Can AI-Generated Rules Be Trusted? What FeatLLM Reveals About Interpretability and Robustness
blogs.description: This article would explore the more interpretability-focused side of the paper. It would discuss how FeatLLM produces human-readable rules, how ensembling and bagging improve robustness, and what the experiments say about resisting spurious correlations. It would also touch on the paper’s caution that LLM prior knowledge can still introduce bias or flawed assumptions.
